title: A plan everyone can enjoy
setup: Two siblings are choosing what to do with their parents.

lines.text: 我們家人都喜歡運動，可是不都喜歡游泳。
lines.pinyin: Wǒmen jiārén dōu xǐhuān yùndòng, kěshì bù dōu xǐhuān yóuyǒng.
lines.translation: Everyone in our family likes exercise, but not everyone likes swimming.
lines.note: 都 covers the whole family. In 不都, the negative comes before 都: only the claim about everyone is denied.
lines.speaker: Older sister

lines.text: 爸爸和媽媽常早上去游泳。我喜歡打籃球。
lines.pinyin: Bàba hé māma cháng zǎoshang qù yóuyǒng. Wǒ xǐhuān dǎ lánqiú.
lines.translation: Dad and Mum often go swimming in the morning. I like playing basketball.
lines.note: Read 爸爸和媽媽 as one subject. 常 marks a habit, not a promise about tomorrow.
lines.speaker: Older sister

lines.text: 我也喜歡打籃球。明天早上我們一起去，好不好？
lines.pinyin: Wǒ yě xǐhuān dǎ lánqiú. Míngtiān zǎoshang wǒmen yìqǐ qù, hǎo bù hǎo?
lines.translation: I like basketball too. Shall we go together tomorrow morning?
lines.note: 也 links the younger sibling’s preference to the older sister’s. 去 leaves the understood basketball activity unspoken.
lines.speaker: Younger sibling

lines.text: 好啊！晚上我們和爸爸、媽媽一起吃晚飯。
lines.pinyin: Hǎo a! Wǎnshang wǒmen hé bàba, māma yìqǐ chī wǎnfàn.
lines.translation: Sure! In the evening we can have dinner together with Dad and Mum.
lines.note: 早上 and 晚上 separate two plans. The dinner group includes the parents; the basketball invitation was between the siblings.
lines.speaker: Older sister

lines.text: 越南菜怎麼樣？我們都喜歡。
lines.pinyin: Yuènán cài zěnmeyàng? Wǒmen dōu xǐhuān.
lines.translation: How about Vietnamese food? We all like it.
lines.note: 菜 means cuisine here. 怎麼樣 asks for a reaction to a suggestion, and the object of 喜歡 is understood.
lines.speaker: Younger sibling

questions.prompt: Which statement fits the family?
options: Everyone likes exercise, but swimming is not a shared preference.
questions.explanation: 不都 does not mean 都不. The parents’ swimming habit also rules out “nobody.”

questions.prompt: Who agrees to play basketball tomorrow morning?
questions.explanation: The younger sibling responds to the older sister’s basketball preference; she accepts the invitation.

questions.prompt: What brings the family together in the evening?
questions.explanation: The evening plan explicitly includes Dad and Mum and uses 吃晚飯.

questions.prompt: Why suggest Vietnamese food?
options: It is something they all like.
questions.explanation: The reason supplied is 我們都喜歡. Price and cooking ability are not mentioned.

tips: Follow changes in the group referred to by 我們. A pronoun can include different people as the conversation moves on.
Distinguish habits (常) from a specific plan (明天早上).
grammarFocus: 好不好 and 怎麼樣

可是.note: The family shares one preference, but not the other.

title: The order and the change
setup: A customer buys a drink and buns. Work out what is ordered, not just the numbers.

lines.text: 老闆，請問一個包子多少錢？
lines.pinyin: Lǎobǎn, qǐngwèn yí ge bāozi duōshǎo qián?
lines.translation: Excuse me, how much is one bun?
lines.note: 老闆 addresses the shopkeeper; 請問 politely introduces the question.
lines.speaker: Customer

lines.text: 一個二十塊。熱茶一杯三十塊。
lines.pinyin: Yí ge èrshí kuài. Rè chá yì bēi sānshí kuài.
lines.translation: One is twenty dollars. A cup of hot tea is thirty dollars.
lines.note: The first reply omits 包子 because it is understood. 個 counts buns; 杯 counts drinks.
lines.speaker: Shopkeeper

lines.text: 我要兩個包子、一杯熱茶。請幫我微波包子。
lines.pinyin: Wǒ yào liǎng ge bāozi, yì bēi rè chá. Qǐng bāng wǒ wéibō bāozi.
lines.translation: I would like two buns and a cup of hot tea. Please microwave the buns for me.
lines.note: 兩 is used before 個. In 幫我微波, 我 is the person receiving help, not the person microwaving.
lines.speaker: Customer

lines.text: 好的。一共七十塊。內用還是外帶？
lines.pinyin: Hǎo de. Yígòng qīshí kuài. Nèiyòng háishì wàidài?
lines.translation: Certainly. Seventy dollars altogether. For here or to go?
lines.note: 一共 introduces the total. 還是 offers two alternatives in a question.
lines.speaker: Shopkeeper

lines.text: 外帶。這是一百塊，謝謝。
lines.pinyin: Wàidài. Zhè shì yì bǎi kuài, xièxie.
lines.translation: To go. Here is one hundred dollars. Thank you.
lines.note: The payment is one hundred; the cost is seventy. Do not treat every amount as a price.
lines.speaker: Customer

questions.prompt: What does the customer buy?
questions.explanation: 兩個包子 means two buns, and 一杯熱茶 means one cup of hot tea. The measure words keep the quantities separate.

questions.prompt: What is the shopkeeper asked to heat?
options: Both the tea and the buns.
questions.explanation: 包子 is the object after 微波. The tea is already described as hot.

questions.prompt: How much change should the customer receive?
questions.explanation: The total is seventy and the payment is one hundred: the difference is thirty.

questions.prompt: Which is definitely true?
options: The order is to take away.
The customer will eat in the shop.
questions.explanation: 外帶 directly answers the shopkeeper’s choice question.

tips: Track what each number measures: unit price, quantity, total, or payment.
Translate 請幫我… as “Please … for me,” rather than word by word.

title: Good at cooking, bad at spicy food
setup: A student compares yesterday’s meal with tonight’s plan.

lines.text: 昨天我和姐姐去一家很有名的餐廳吃牛肉麵。
lines.pinyin: Zuótiān wǒ hé jiějie qù yì jiā hěn yǒumíng de cāntīng chī niúròu miàn.
lines.translation: Yesterday my older sister and I went to a famous restaurant for beef noodles.
lines.note: The time comes first; 去 + place + action tells both destination and purpose.

lines.text: 姐姐覺得麵真好吃，可是我怕辣。
lines.pinyin: Jiějie juéde miàn zhēn hǎochī, kěshì wǒ pà là.
lines.translation: My sister thought the noodles were really good, but I am sensitive to spicy food.
lines.note: 可是 contrasts two people’s experiences. 怕辣 describes sensitivity, not whether a dish is physically hot.

lines.text: 湯有一點辣，所以我不想喝。
lines.pinyin: Tāng yǒu yìdiǎn là, suǒyǐ wǒ bù xiǎng hē.
lines.translation: The broth was a little spicy, so I did not want to drink it.
lines.note: 有一點 softens a negative assessment. 所以 introduces its consequence; the understood object of 喝 is 湯.

lines.text: 今天晚上姐姐想自己做飯。她做飯做得很好，也會做甜點。
lines.pinyin: Jīntiān wǎnshang jiějie xiǎng zìjǐ zuòfàn. Tā zuòfàn zuò de hěn hǎo, yě huì zuò tiándiǎn.
lines.translation: Tonight my sister wants to cook herself. She cooks very well and can make desserts too.
lines.note: 做飯做得很好 repeats the verb after the object 飯. 得 introduces how well she cooks; 會 says she has a skill.

lines.text: 我不會做甜點。我想學，姐姐可以教我。
lines.pinyin: Wǒ bú huì zuò tiándiǎn. Wǒ xiǎng xué, jiějie kěyǐ jiāo wǒ.
lines.translation: I cannot make desserts. I want to learn, and my sister can teach me.
lines.note: The omitted skill after 學 and 教 is making desserts, supplied by the preceding sentence.

questions.prompt: Why did the narrator avoid the broth?
questions.explanation: The narrator is sensitive to spice; the broth’s spiciness is the stated reason.

questions.prompt: What is planned for tonight?
options: Another meal at the same restaurant.
questions.explanation: 今天晚上 introduces the new plan; the restaurant visit was yesterday.

questions.prompt: What does 做飯做得很好 tell us beyond 會做飯?
options: She cooks well, not merely that she can cook.
questions.explanation: 得很好 evaluates performance; 會 expresses learned ability.

questions.prompt: What would the narrator like to learn?
questions.explanation: The missing object of 學 refers back to 做甜點.

tips: Chinese often leaves out an object that is obvious from context. Look backward before assuming a new activity.
Keep temperature (熱) separate from spiciness (辣).

得.meaning: links an action to how it is done

title: Where is your friend?
setup: A visitor arrives near a friend’s school.

lines.text: 我現在在你學校外面。你在家嗎？
lines.pinyin: Wǒ xiànzài zài nǐ xuéxiào wàimiàn. Nǐ zài jiā ma?
lines.translation: I am outside your school now. Are you at home?
lines.note: 現在 is time; 在 introduces location. 學校外面 is outside the school, not inside it.
lines.speaker: Visitor

lines.text: 我不在家，我在圖書館看書。你到這裡來找我吧。
lines.pinyin: Wǒ bú zài jiā, wǒ zài túshūguǎn kàn shū. Nǐ dào zhèlǐ lái zhǎo wǒ ba.
lines.translation: I am not at home; I am reading in the library. Come here to meet me.
lines.note: The second 在 puts reading in a location. 到這裡來 directs the visitor toward the speaker.
lines.speaker: Friend

lines.text: 圖書館在哪裡？遠不遠？
lines.pinyin: Túshūguǎn zài nǎlǐ? Yuǎn bù yuǎn?
lines.translation: Where is the library? Is it far?
lines.note: 遠不遠 asks about distance. It does not say the library is far.
lines.speaker: Visitor

lines.text: 在學校裡面，很近。附近也有商店，可以買東西。
lines.pinyin: Zài xuéxiào lǐmiàn, hěn jìn. Fùjìn yě yǒu shāngdiàn, kěyǐ mǎi dōngxi.
lines.translation: It is inside the school, very close. There are shops nearby too, where you can buy things.
lines.note: The omitted subject is the library. 有 introduces what exists nearby; it does not locate the friend in a shop.
lines.speaker: Friend

lines.text: 好，我去找你。今天晚上一起吃飯，怎麼樣？
lines.pinyin: Hǎo, wǒ qù zhǎo nǐ. Jīntiān wǎnshang yìqǐ chīfàn, zěnmeyàng?
lines.translation: Okay, I will come and meet you. How about having dinner together tonight?
lines.note: 去 follows the visitor’s viewpoint: going away from the visitor’s current location. The dinner is still a suggestion.
lines.speaker: Visitor

questions.prompt: Where is the friend now?
questions.explanation: 我在圖書館看書 explicitly locates the friend.

questions.prompt: Which movement matches the invitation?
options: From outside the school to the library inside.
From a shop to a restaurant.
From the library to the visitor’s home.
questions.explanation: The visitor is outside; the friend invites them to the library inside the school.

questions.prompt: Why are the shops mentioned?
options: To point out a convenient place to buy things.
To identify where the friend is reading.
To say the library sells food.
questions.explanation: 可以買東西 gives the purpose of mentioning nearby shops.

questions.prompt: Which detail is still only a proposal?
questions.explanation: 怎麼樣 invites a response; no acceptance is included in these messages.

tips: Resolve 這裡 from the speaker’s location, not the reader’s location.
Separate stated facts from questions and proposals.

title: The afternoon that does not fit
setup: A student writes down an afternoon schedule before choosing a meeting time.

lines.text: 今天下午一點到兩點，我有中文課。兩點半到三點半，我有書法課。
lines.pinyin: Jīntiān xiàwǔ yì diǎn dào liǎng diǎn, wǒ yǒu Zhōngwén kè. Liǎng diǎn bàn dào sān diǎn bàn, wǒ yǒu shūfǎ kè.
lines.translation: Today I have Chinese from one to two and calligraphy from half past two to half past three.
lines.note: 到 connects the endpoints of each time range. 半 after 點 means half past.

lines.text: 學校的籃球比賽三點開始，四點半結束。
lines.pinyin: Xuéxiào de lánqiú bǐsài sān diǎn kāishǐ, sì diǎn bàn jiéshù.
lines.translation: The school’s basketball game starts at three and ends at half past four.
lines.note: The game is the subject of both 開始 and 結束; the time precedes each verb.

lines.text: 朋友想兩點半和我見面，一起去看比賽。
lines.pinyin: Péngyǒu xiǎng liǎng diǎn bàn hé wǒ jiànmiàn, yìqǐ qù kàn bǐsài.
lines.translation: My friend wants to meet me at half past two and go to watch the game together.
lines.note: 想 marks the friend’s proposed plan, not an agreed appointment.

lines.text: 可是我兩點半在教室上課。我四點有空，可以在圖書館前面見面。
lines.pinyin: Kěshì wǒ liǎng diǎn bàn zài jiàoshì shàngkè. Wǒ sì diǎn yǒukòng, kěyǐ zài túshūguǎn qiánmiàn jiànmiàn.
lines.translation: But at half past two I will be in class. I am free at four; we can meet in front of the library.
lines.note: Time comes before place, then activity. 在教室 locates the class; it is not the progressive 在 + action pattern.

lines.text: 朋友說：「好，我們四點見。」
lines.pinyin: Péngyǒu shuō: “Hǎo, wǒmen sì diǎn jiàn.”
lines.translation: My friend says, “Okay, see you at four.”
lines.note: The friend accepts the later time. Do not keep the rejected half-past-two time as the final plan.

questions.prompt: What prevents the proposed 2:30 meeting?
questions.explanation: Chinese ends at two; calligraphy starts at half past two.

questions.prompt: At the agreed meeting time, what is true of the game?
questions.explanation: Four o’clock falls between its three o’clock start and four-thirty finish.

questions.prompt: Where do they plan to meet?
questions.explanation: 圖書館前面 means in front of the library. 在教室 belongs to the earlier class, not the meeting.

questions.prompt: Which time is the final agreement?
questions.explanation: The final quoted reply confirms four o’clock.

tips: Read all messages before choosing a meeting time: a proposed time can be replaced.
Use the time ranges to infer conflicts; a comprehension question may require combining two sentences.

見.meaning: see; meet (short for 見面 here)

title: Fast is not the only reason
setup: Two friends compare ways to get to school.

lines.text: 今天我們坐捷運還是坐公車去學校？
lines.pinyin: Jīntiān wǒmen zuò jiéyùn háishì zuò gōngchē qù xuéxiào?
lines.translation: Shall we take the MRT or the bus to school today?
lines.note: 還是 asks the listener to choose between transport options.
lines.speaker: A

lines.text: 捷運比公車快，可是公車比較便宜。
lines.pinyin: Jiéyùn bǐ gōngchē kuài, kěshì gōngchē bǐjiào piányí.
lines.translation: The MRT is faster than the bus, but the bus is cheaper.
lines.note: 比 names both sides of a comparison. 比較 can leave the comparison understood. Fastest and cheapest need not be the same choice.
lines.speaker: B

lines.text: 你家附近有捷運站嗎？
lines.pinyin: Nǐ jiā fùjìn yǒu jiéyùn zhàn ma?
lines.translation: Is there an MRT station near your home?
lines.note: 附近 sets a location for 有. The question supplies no answer by itself.
lines.speaker: A

lines.text: 沒有。公車站很近，坐公車很方便。
lines.pinyin: Méiyǒu. Gōngchē zhàn hěn jìn, zuò gōngchē hěn fāngbiàn.
lines.translation: No. The bus stop is very close, so taking the bus is convenient.
lines.note: 沒有 answers the station question. The convenience claim is about the bus, not the MRT.
lines.speaker: B

lines.text: 好，我們今天坐公車。明天一起騎機車，好不好？
lines.pinyin: Hǎo, wǒmen jīntiān zuò gōngchē. Míngtiān yìqǐ qí jīchē, hǎo bù hǎo?
lines.translation: Okay, let’s take the bus today. Shall we ride scooters together tomorrow?
lines.note: 今天 settles the bus plan; 明天 introduces a separate scooter suggestion. 好不好 asks for agreement.
lines.speaker: A

questions.prompt: Which option is described as faster?
questions.explanation: 捷運比公車快 explicitly compares the MRT with the bus.

questions.prompt: Why does the bus make sense for today?
options: It is cheaper and the stop is close.
There is no bus stop nearby.
It is faster than the MRT.
questions.explanation: The text supplies both cost and convenience reasons.

questions.prompt: Is an MRT station near B’s home?
questions.explanation: 沒有 is the short negative answer to 有…嗎.

questions.prompt: What is suggested for tomorrow?
questions.explanation: The scooter suggestion belongs to 明天, not today’s journey.

tips: Follow the comparison direction: A 比 B 快 means A is faster.
A travel choice can combine cost, distance to a stop, and speed.

站.note: 捷運站 is an MRT station; 公車站 is a bus stop.

title: Two days, one afternoon
setup: A student explains why a short visit will not be too busy.

lines.text: 我下星期打算到朋友家去，玩兩天。
lines.pinyin: Wǒ xià xīngqí dǎsuàn dào péngyǒu jiā qù, wán liǎng tiān.
lines.translation: Next week I plan to visit a friend for two days.
lines.note: 下星期 says when; 兩天 after 玩 says how long the visit’s activities last.

lines.text: 坐火車要兩個鐘頭，坐公共汽車要三個鐘頭。
lines.pinyin: Zuò huǒchē yào liǎng ge zhōngtóu, zuò gōnggòng qìchē yào sān ge zhōngtóu.
lines.translation: The train takes two hours; the bus takes three.
lines.note: 要 before a duration means the journey requires that amount of time.

lines.text: 朋友建議我坐火車。我也覺得火車比較快，所以決定坐火車。
lines.pinyin: Péngyǒu jiànyì wǒ zuò huǒchē. Wǒ yě juéde huǒchē bǐjiào kuài, suǒyǐ juédìng zuò huǒchē.
lines.translation: My friend suggests the train. I also think it is faster, so I decide to take it.
lines.note: 建議 introduces someone else’s advice; 決定 identifies the narrator’s final decision.

lines.text: 朋友下午有課。我在他上課的時候看書，晚上一起去夜市。
lines.pinyin: Péngyǒu xiàwǔ yǒu kè. Wǒ zài tā shàngkè de shíhòu kàn shū, wǎnshang yìqǐ qù yèshì.
lines.translation: My friend has class in the afternoon. I will read while he is in class; in the evening we will go to the night market together.
lines.note: 他上課的時候 is a time clause. The afternoon reading and evening visit belong to different parts of the day.

lines.text: 我不想每天都出去玩。有時候在家聽音樂，也非常好。
lines.pinyin: Wǒ bù xiǎng měitiān dōu chūqù wán. Yǒushíhòu zài jiā tīng yīnyuè, yě fēicháng hǎo.
lines.translation: I do not want to go out for fun every day. Sometimes listening to music at home is very nice too.
lines.note: 不想 denies the desire for daily outings. It does not mean the narrator refuses every outing.

questions.prompt: How long is the planned stay?
questions.explanation: 玩兩天 gives the visit’s duration; the hours describe transport.

questions.prompt: Why choose the train?
questions.explanation: Two hours is shorter than three, and the narrator explicitly says 比較快.

questions.prompt: What will the narrator do during the friend’s class?
questions.explanation: 看書 is the main activity linked to 他上課的時候.

questions.prompt: Which summary best fits the plan?
options: Stay home and never meet the friend.
Combine one outing with quieter time.
Go out all day every day.
questions.explanation: The night market outing and at-home activities both form part of the plan.

tips: Do not confuse a journey duration with the length of a stay.
Read an entire …的時候 clause as “when/while …” before translating the main action.

title: Find the right person
setup: Someone explains a photo to a friend who has not met their family.

lines.text: 上個月我們在旅館外面拍照片。這張照片裡有我姐姐、弟弟和一個朋友。
lines.pinyin: Shàng ge yuè wǒmen zài lǚguǎn wàimiàn pāi zhàopiàn. Zhè zhāng zhàopiàn lǐ yǒu wǒ jiějie, dìdi hé yí ge péngyǒu.
lines.translation: Last month we took photos outside a hotel. This photo shows my older sister, younger brother, and a friend.
lines.note: Time comes before place and action. 照片裡有 introduces the people shown in the picture.

lines.text: 穿藍色衣服的人是我姐姐。她很高，笑得很開心。
lines.pinyin: Chuān lánsè yīfu de rén shì wǒ jiějie. Tā hěn gāo, xiào de hěn kāixīn.
lines.translation: The person wearing blue is my older sister. She is tall and is smiling happily.
lines.note: 穿藍色衣服 modifies 人 through 的. Read the whole modifier before deciding who is identified.

lines.text: 我弟弟穿紅色的衣服。他不笑，因為他不喜歡照相。
lines.pinyin: Wǒ dìdi chuān hóngsè de yīfu. Tā bù xiào, yīnwèi tā bù xǐhuān zhàoxiàng.
lines.translation: My younger brother is wearing red. He is not smiling because he dislikes having his photo taken.
lines.note: 因為 explains the absence of a smile. It does not establish that he dislikes the people or the hotel.

lines.text: 在窗戶前面的人是我的朋友。他的衣服也是藍色的。
lines.pinyin: Zài chuānghù qiánmiàn de rén shì wǒ de péngyǒu. Tā de yīfu yě shì lánsè de.
lines.translation: The person in front of the window is my friend. His clothes are blue too.
lines.note: The location clause identifies the friend. 也 shows that blue clothing is shared by two people.

lines.text: 你要找我姐姐？穿藍色衣服的有兩個人，她是很高的那個。
lines.pinyin: Nǐ yào zhǎo wǒ jiějie? Chuān lánsè yīfu de yǒu liǎng ge rén, tā shì hěn gāo de nà ge.
lines.translation: Are you looking for my sister? Two people are wearing blue; she is the tall one.
lines.note: 的 lets the clothing description stand for people. 很高的那個 adds the distinguishing clue, with 人 understood.

questions.prompt: Who wears blue?
questions.explanation: The friend’s clothes are blue 也, in addition to the sister’s.

questions.prompt: Why is the brother not smiling?
options: He is angry with his sister.
questions.explanation: The 因為 clause gives only the photography reason.

questions.prompt: Which clue identifies the friend?
options: Standing in front of the window.
questions.explanation: The window location identifies the friend directly.

questions.prompt: Why is clothing colour insufficient to find the sister?
options: Someone else is wearing blue too.
questions.explanation: Two people share the same colour, so a second clue is needed.

tips: A modifier can be a full clause: [穿藍色衣服] + 的 + 人.
Combine clues instead of stopping at the first matching word.

的.meaning: links a description to its noun, or stands for the understood noun

title: A room for a long plan
setup: A student considers a room while planning their studies.

lines.text: 我計畫先在語言中心念中文，再念大學，所以需要在學校附近租房間。
lines.pinyin: Wǒ jìhuà xiān zài yǔyán zhōngxīn niàn Zhōngwén, zài niàn dàxué, suǒyǐ xūyào zài xuéxiào fùjìn zū fángjiān.
lines.translation: I plan to study Chinese at a language centre first, then attend university, so I need to rent a room near school.
lines.note: 先…再… orders the study stages. 所以 connects the study plan with the housing need.

lines.text: 這間套房不大，可是很乾淨。廚房在左邊，浴室在右邊。
lines.pinyin: Zhè jiān tàofáng bú dà, kěshì hěn gānjìng. Chúfáng zài zuǒbiān, yùshì zài yòubiān.
lines.translation: This studio is not big, but it is clean. The kitchen is on the left and the bathroom on the right.
lines.note: 間 counts rooms. 不大 is a limitation; 可是 shifts to a favourable feature.

lines.text: 走路五分鐘就到學校，買東西也很方便。
lines.pinyin: Zǒulù wǔ fēnzhōng jiù dào xuéxiào, mǎi dōngxi yě hěn fāngbiàn.
lines.translation: It takes only five minutes to walk to school, and shopping is convenient too.
lines.note: 五分鐘 is a duration, not five o’clock. 就 presents reaching school as quick and convenient.

lines.text: 不過熱水器好像有問題。房東說明天下午來看。
lines.pinyin: Búguò rèshuǐqì hǎoxiàng yǒu wèntí. Fángdōng shuō míngtiān xiàwǔ lái kàn.
lines.translation: However, the water heater seems to have a problem. The landlord says they will come and look tomorrow afternoon.
lines.note: 好像 marks an impression, not a confirmed diagnosis. 來看 leaves the water heater understood as the object.

lines.text: 我還沒有決定。房間不錯，可是我想先問房租，再決定。
lines.pinyin: Wǒ hái méiyǒu juédìng. Fángjiān búcuò, kěshì wǒ xiǎng xiān wèn fángzū, zài juédìng.
lines.translation: I have not decided yet. The room is nice, but I want to ask about the rent before deciding.
lines.note: 還沒有 means not yet. The second 先…再… describes the next decision steps, not the earlier study plan.

questions.prompt: What comes first in the study plan?
questions.explanation: 先 marks Chinese study; 再 introduces university afterward.

questions.prompt: What makes the location appealing?
options: It is a short walk from school.
questions.explanation: The five-minute walk and convenient shopping support the location choice.

questions.prompt: What is uncertain about the water heater?
options: Whether the landlord will sell it.
Whether it really has a problem.
questions.explanation: 好像 presents a suspected problem; the landlord has not inspected it yet.

questions.prompt: Has the student agreed to rent it?
options: Yes, but only for one night.
Yes, the rent is already paid.
No; they want to ask the rent first.
questions.explanation: 還沒有決定 explicitly says the decision is pending.

tips: Words such as 好像 and 還沒有 limit how certain a conclusion can be.
Translate 就 in context: here “only” captures the unexpectedly short travel time.

分鐘.note: 五分鐘 is five minutes. Use 點 for hours on a clock, such as 五點 (five o’clock).

title: A birthday between work and study
setup: A student replies to a friend’s birthday invitation.

lines.text: 好久不見！我記得明天是你的生日。生日快樂！
lines.pinyin: Hǎojiǔ bú jiàn! Wǒ jìde míngtiān shì nǐ de shēngrì. Shēngrì kuàilè!
lines.translation: Long time no see! I remember your birthday is tomorrow. Happy birthday!
lines.note: 記得 reports remembering; 明天 sets the birthday in the future.

lines.text: 我最近很忙。早上上班，下午念中文，晚上做功課。
lines.pinyin: Wǒ zuìjìn hěn máng. Zǎoshang shàngbān, xiàwǔ niàn Zhōngwén, wǎnshang zuò gōngkè.
lines.translation: I have been busy lately: work in the morning, Chinese study in the afternoon, and homework in the evening.
lines.note: The subject 我 is shared across the three time phrases. Chinese does not need to repeat it each time.

lines.text: 我的學費是自己付的，所以我需要工作。
lines.pinyin: Wǒ de xuéfèi shì zìjǐ fù de, suǒyǐ wǒ xūyào gōngzuò.
lines.translation: I paid my tuition myself, so I need to work.
lines.note: 是…的 focuses on who paid: 自己. It does not mean the payment is a future plan.

lines.text: 明天我五點下課，六點可以到你家。你想在家吃飯，還是出去吃？
lines.pinyin: Míngtiān wǒ wǔ diǎn xiàkè, liù diǎn kěyǐ dào nǐ jiā. Nǐ xiǎng zài jiā chīfàn, háishì chūqù chī?
lines.translation: Tomorrow class ends at five, and I can reach your home at six. Would you like to eat at home or go out?
lines.note: 下課 and 到 describe separate events at separate times. 還是 leaves the meal location for the friend to choose.

lines.text: 吃飯以後，我就回來。後天早上有工作，我不想太累。
lines.pinyin: Chīfàn yǐhòu, wǒ jiù huílái. Hòutiān zǎoshang yǒu gōngzuò, wǒ bù xiǎng tài lèi.
lines.translation: After dinner I will come straight back. I have work the next morning and do not want to be too tired.
lines.note: 吃飯以後 marks the later action. 就 makes the return follow dinner directly; the next morning’s work supplies the reason.

questions.prompt: Why does the writer need to work?
questions.explanation: The 是…的 sentence identifies the payer; 所以 connects that fact to work.

questions.prompt: When can the writer reach the friend’s home?
questions.explanation: Five is the end of class; six is the arrival time.

questions.prompt: What has not been chosen yet?
options: Whether to eat at home or outside.
questions.explanation: The 還是 question leaves this choice open.

questions.prompt: What limits the writer’s evening?
questions.explanation: The final sentence provides the reason for returning after dinner.

tips: In 是…的, identify the focused information rather than reading it as a plain identity statement.
Separate what a message confirms from what it asks the other person to decide.

上班.meaning: go to work; be at work

title: Not everyone wants the same dinner
setup: Two friends are organising a birthday meal for another friend.

lines.text: 明天他生日，我訂了豬腳和麵線。蛋呢？
lines.pinyin: Míngtiān tā shēngrì, wǒ dìng le zhūjiǎo hé miànxiàn. Dàn ne?
lines.translation: It is his birthday tomorrow. I have ordered pork knuckle and thin noodles. What about eggs?
lines.note: 了 follows 訂 to mark a completed order. The birthday itself is still tomorrow.
lines.speaker: A

lines.text: 我買了，可是他不吃蛋。
lines.pinyin: Wǒ mǎi le, kěshì tā bù chī dàn.
lines.translation: I bought some, but he does not eat eggs.
lines.note: The object after 買 is omitted because the question supplied eggs. 不吃 describes a preference or habit.
lines.speaker: B

lines.text: 真的？他不是什麼都吃嗎？
lines.pinyin: Zhēn de? Tā bú shì shénme dōu chī ma?
lines.translation: Really? Doesn’t he eat everything?
lines.note: 什麼都吃 means eat everything. The final 嗎 turns the speaker’s assumption into a question.
lines.speaker: A

lines.text: 不是。他喜歡吃麵線，也喜歡豬腳。那些蛋，我自己吃。
lines.pinyin: Bú shì. Tā xǐhuān chī miànxiàn, yě xǐhuān zhūjiǎo. Nàxiē dàn, wǒ zìjǐ chī.
lines.translation: No. He likes thin noodles and pork knuckle. Those eggs are for me.
lines.note: 不是 rejects the “everything” assumption. 那些蛋 is the topic; 我自己 identifies who will eat them.
lines.speaker: B

lines.text: 那我們多買一點水果吧。我們都可以吃。
lines.pinyin: Nà wǒmen duō mǎi yìdiǎn shuǐguǒ ba. Wǒmen dōu kěyǐ chī.
lines.translation: Then let’s buy a little more fruit. We can all have some.
lines.note: 多 before 買 means buy more; 一點 limits the extra amount. 吧 makes this a suggestion.
lines.speaker: A

questions.prompt: Which food has A already ordered?
questions.explanation: 訂了 marks the order as complete and lists both foods.

questions.prompt: Who will eat the eggs?
questions.explanation: B explicitly says the eggs are for themself.

questions.prompt: What assumption is corrected?
options: That the birthday friend eats everything.
questions.explanation: 什麼都吃 is rejected by 不是 and the egg preference.

questions.prompt: What remains a suggestion, rather than a completed purchase?
questions.explanation: The eggs were bought and the meal ordered; 多買一點水果吧 proposes another purchase.

tips: Keep 不吃 (a preference) separate from 沒吃 (an event did not happen).
Question words with 都 can mean “everything/everyone,” without asking a question.

title: A walk that can wait
setup: Friends revise a plan after checking the weather.

lines.text: 我們昨天決定今天下午去山上看風景。可是新聞說颱風快要來了。
lines.pinyin: Wǒmen zuótiān juédìng jīntiān xiàwǔ qù shānshàng kàn fēngjǐng. Kěshì xīnwén shuō táifēng kuài yào lái le.
lines.translation: Yesterday we decided to go into the mountains this afternoon for the scenery. But the news says a typhoon is about to arrive.
lines.note: 昨天 locates the decision; 今天下午 locates the planned outing. 快要…了 marks the typhoon as approaching.

lines.text: 早上下了兩個鐘頭的雨，現在還沒停。外面的風也比昨天更大。
lines.pinyin: Zǎoshang xià le liǎng ge zhōngtóu de yǔ, xiànzài hái méi tíng. Wàimiàn de fēng yě bǐ zuótiān gèng dà.
lines.translation: It rained for two hours in the morning and still has not stopped. The wind outside is even stronger than yesterday.
lines.note: 下了…雨 puts a duration between verb and noun. 還沒停 says it continues; 比…更 adds emphasis to the comparison.

lines.text: 朋友帶了傘，說：「有傘就可以出去吧？」
lines.pinyin: Péngyǒu dài le sǎn, shuō: “Yǒu sǎn jiù kěyǐ chūqù ba?”
lines.translation: My friend brought an umbrella and says, “With an umbrella, we can go out, right?”
lines.note: 帶了 is completed. The final 吧 seeks agreement with a guess; it does not prove the plan is sensible.

lines.text: 我說：「今天沒有昨天那麼冷，可是風更大。山上太可怕了，我們不要去。」
lines.pinyin: Wǒ shuō: “Jīntiān méiyǒu zuótiān nàme lěng, kěshì fēng gèng dà. Shānshàng tài kěpà le, wǒmen bú yào qù.”
lines.translation: I say, “Today is not as cold as yesterday, but the wind is stronger. The mountains would be too scary; let’s not go.”
lines.note: 沒有…那麼冷 compares temperature. It does not say the whole day’s weather is better.

lines.text: 我們決定在家看電影。雨停了以後，再去附近買晚飯。
lines.pinyin: Wǒmen juédìng zài jiā kàn diànyǐng. Yǔ tíng le yǐhòu, zài qù fùjìn mǎi wǎnfàn.
lines.translation: We decide to watch a film at home. After the rain stops, we will go nearby to buy dinner.
lines.note: 再 gives the later action in the revised plan. 雨停了以後 sets a future condition here, rather than claiming the rain has already stopped.

questions.prompt: What changes the original mountain plan?
options: The approaching typhoon and strong wind.
questions.explanation: The news and worsening wind are the stated reasons for staying home.

questions.prompt: Compared with yesterday, today is…
questions.explanation: 沒有昨天那麼冷 and 風更大 describe two different comparisons.

questions.prompt: What mistake does the umbrella suggestion make?
options: It assumes the rain has stopped.
It treats having an umbrella as enough to make the outing possible.
It assumes nobody brought an umbrella.
questions.explanation: The reply points to stronger wind despite the umbrella.

questions.prompt: When do they plan to buy dinner?
questions.explanation: 雨停了以後 states the timing condition, not a completed event.

tips: Compare one property at a time: less cold does not imply better weather overall.
A 了 clause inside a future plan can describe an event that must finish before another action.

title: Feeling better is not the same as well
setup: A student checks on a friend who has been ill. Read the symptoms and the plans carefully.

lines.text: 你昨天一直流鼻水，今天怎麼樣？要不要一起去打籃球？
lines.pinyin: Nǐ zuótiān yìzhí liú bíshuǐ, jīntiān zěnmeyàng? Yào bú yào yìqǐ qù dǎ lánqiú?
lines.translation: Your nose kept running yesterday. How are you today? Do you want to play basketball together?
lines.note: 一直 describes continuation yesterday. The question asks about today; it does not establish recovery.
lines.speaker: A

lines.text: 鼻水少一點了，可是頭還很痛。醫生說是感冒，要多喝水、多休息。
lines.pinyin: Bíshuǐ shǎo yìdiǎn le, kěshì tóu hái hěn tòng. Yīshēng shuō shì gǎnmào, yào duō hē shuǐ, duō xiūxi.
lines.translation: The runny nose is a little better, but my head still really hurts. The doctor says it is a cold and I should drink more water and rest more.
lines.note: 少一點了 marks a small change, not full recovery. 多 before a verb advises doing more of the activity.
lines.speaker: B

lines.text: 那最好別去了。你拿藥了嗎？我可以陪你去藥局。
lines.pinyin: Nà zuìhǎo bié qù le. Nǐ ná yào le ma? Wǒ kěyǐ péi nǐ qù yàojú.
lines.translation: Then it is best not to go. Have you picked up your medicine? I can go with you to the pharmacy.
lines.note: 那 responds to the symptoms. 最好別 gives advice; 可以陪 is an offer, not a completed trip.
lines.speaker: A

lines.text: 謝謝，不用了。我昨天就拿了藥。今天吃了午餐就吃藥，下午在家睡覺。
lines.pinyin: Xièxie, bú yòng le. Wǒ zuótiān jiù ná le yào. Jīntiān chī le wǔcān jiù chī yào, xiàwǔ zài jiā shuìjiào.
lines.translation: Thanks, there is no need. I picked up the medicine yesterday. Today I will take it right after lunch and sleep at home in the afternoon.
lines.note: 昨天就拿了 explains the polite refusal. 吃了午餐就吃藥 orders two actions in today’s plan; it is this character’s plan, not general medical advice.
lines.speaker: B

lines.text: 好，我晚上再來看你。你休息吧，別一直看手機。
lines.pinyin: Hǎo, wǒ wǎnshang zài lái kàn nǐ. Nǐ xiūxi ba, bié yìzhí kàn shǒujī.
lines.translation: Okay, I will come and see you this evening. Rest, and do not keep looking at your phone.
lines.note: 再 moves the visit to later. 別一直 negates continuing an activity, rather than banning the object itself.
lines.speaker: A

lines.text: 好。今天我想比昨天早一點睡。謝謝你關心我。
lines.pinyin: Hǎo. Jīntiān wǒ xiǎng bǐ zuótiān zǎo yìdiǎn shuì. Xièxie nǐ guānxīn wǒ.
lines.translation: Okay. I want to go to sleep a little earlier than yesterday. Thank you for caring about me.
lines.note: 比昨天 supplies the comparison and 一點 makes the change modest. 關心 means showing care, not asking a factual question.
lines.speaker: B

questions.prompt: Which description best fits B’s condition?
options: One symptom has eased, but a headache remains.
questions.explanation: 少一點了 signals improvement in the runny nose, while 頭還很痛 states a remaining problem.

questions.prompt: Why does B decline the pharmacy offer?
questions.explanation: 昨天就拿了藥 gives the explicit reason for 不用了.

questions.prompt: What is B’s stated sequence today?
questions.explanation: 吃了午餐就吃藥 places medicine after lunch; afternoon sleep follows.

questions.prompt: What will A do instead of playing basketball with B?
options: Take B to the pharmacy immediately.
questions.explanation: The later visit replaces the initial sports suggestion.

tips: Read degree words precisely: 一點 indicates a little, not a complete change.
A polite 不用了 can decline a specific offer while still expressing gratitude.
grammarFocus: 最好別 and 多 + verb

多.meaning: more; do more of the following activity (here)

title: The shop you walk past
setup: Two students are trying to find a noodle shop. No external map is needed.

lines.text: 我下載了地圖，可是不知道麵店在哪裡。你可以幫忙嗎？
lines.pinyin: Wǒ xiàzài le dìtú, kěshì bù zhīdào miàndiàn zài nǎlǐ. Nǐ kěyǐ bāngmáng ma?
lines.translation: I downloaded a map, but I do not know where the noodle shop is. Can you help?
lines.note: 了 marks the download as complete. 可是 contrasts having the map with still needing help.
lines.speaker: A

lines.text: 你現在看見什麼？附近有紅綠燈嗎？
lines.pinyin: Nǐ xiànzài kànjiàn shénme? Fùjìn yǒu hónglǜdēng ma?
lines.translation: What can you see now? Are there traffic lights nearby?
lines.note: 看見 focuses on what is visible. The questions establish a starting point.
lines.speaker: B

lines.text: 有。我在郵局前面，拿著地圖。背包裡有我買的日用品。
lines.pinyin: Yǒu. Wǒ zài yóujú qiánmiàn, ná zhe dìtú. Bēibāo lǐ yǒu wǒ mǎi de rìyòngpǐn.
lines.translation: Yes. I am in front of the post office, holding the map. My backpack contains the everyday supplies I bought.
lines.note: 拿著 describes continuing to hold the map. 我買的 modifies 日用品: the supplies that I bought.
lines.speaker: A

lines.text: 從郵局往前走，到第一個路口右轉。你會經過一家超商，麵店在超商後面的巷子裡。
lines.pinyin: Cóng yóujú wǎng qián zǒu, dào dì yī ge lùkǒu yòuzhuǎn. Nǐ huì jīngguò yì jiā chāoshāng, miàndiàn zài chāoshāng hòumiàn de xiàngzi lǐ.
lines.translation: Walk forward from the post office and turn right at the first intersection. You will pass a convenience store; the noodle shop is in the lane behind it.
lines.note: 從 marks the start, 到 the turning point, and 後面 locates the lane relative to the store. Passing the store is not the same as stopping there.
lines.speaker: B

lines.text: 麵店離郵局這麼近！我一邊走，一邊看地圖，沒有看見超商後面的巷子。
lines.pinyin: Miàndiàn lí yóujú zhème jìn! Wǒ yìbiān zǒu, yìbiān kàn dìtú, méiyǒu kànjiàn chāoshāng hòumiàn de xiàngzi.
lines.translation: The noodle shop is this close to the post office! I was looking at the map as I walked and did not see the lane behind the convenience store.
lines.note: 離 relates the two places. 一邊…一邊… makes walking and reading simultaneous; 沒有看見 reports a missed landmark.
lines.speaker: A

lines.text: 別一直看地圖，小心。到麵店再打電話給我，我也餓了。
lines.pinyin: Bié yìzhí kàn dìtú, xiǎoxīn. Dào miàndiàn zài dǎ diànhuà gěi wǒ, wǒ yě è le.
lines.translation: Do not keep looking at the map; be careful. Call me when you get to the noodle shop. I am hungry too.
lines.note: 再 delays the call until arrival. 餓了 marks becoming hungry; it does not say B is already at the shop.
lines.speaker: B

questions.prompt: Where is A when asking for help?
options: In front of the post office.
questions.explanation: A explicitly gives the post-office location.

questions.prompt: What is the route from that starting point?
options: Right immediately, without reaching an intersection.
Forward, then right at the first intersection.
questions.explanation: 到第一個路口右轉 places the turn at the first intersection.

questions.prompt: Why does passing the convenience store not finish the journey?
options: The noodle shop is in the lane behind the store.
They must go to another town.
The shop is inside the post office.
questions.explanation: The store is a landmark on the way; the lane behind it is the destination area.

questions.prompt: When does B ask A to call?
questions.explanation: 到麵店再… postpones the call until arrival.

tips: Track landmark relations from the named starting point; do not invent a compass direction for 往前.
Distinguish a continuing state (著), simultaneous actions (一邊…一邊…), and a later action (再).
